questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good studying environment along with a not too busy city or tight school schedule.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult because the school pages on the internet were difficult to navigate, but once I found out it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assisstance from my tutor, teachers and friends.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to find the off campus housing, as it is only about a kilometer away fom the school.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You need to be prepared to buy a lot of different things, as not everything is accomodated for, such as a kettle, pot and pan in single person rooms, along with buying several different types of plastic bags for garbage sorting.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing at first, but easy enough once you got the hang on things.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mainly officials, friends and school guides.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, getting every class that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to do a bit of research before applying to the courses, as it can get confusing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally I'd recommend the courses that teaches you about Japanese history and culture, as it can really help with how the Japanese sees things and how to act.

questions.answer: Vegetables were a lot more expensive than I expected, but besides that, everything is extremely cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tea ceremonies, ping pong, football, dancing and music

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above, as they can help bonding with friends and the Japanese.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Relaxing to recharge for school or hang out with friends during the weekends and shorter breaks, but during the longer breaks, I recommend travelling with friends or family.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy for me to adjust to the cultural change, as I already knew a lot about Japanese culture before I departed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try and approach them your own way and see if you share any interests.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any particularly challenging, but it was a bit peculiar having to be on the left side of the road.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness towards everyone along with its different types of food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to prepare yourself before you travel to Japan, make sure you know how to act and treat others, and make sure you have the money to cover all expenses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you get a bicycle to get around and have money and student id on you at all times in case of emergencies and also make sure to form a few connections.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience Japan for five months and make many friends along with experiencing the culture, sights and traditions of Japan.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to not feel homesick and make friends in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
